title: Freezes on Linux (Wayland) when trying to close windows or when tooltips are shown/hidden.
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: - Godot v4.6.rc1 - Godot v4.6.beta3 ### System information Godot v4.6.rc1 - Ubuntu 25.10 25.10 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (nvidia; 580.95.05) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10400F CPU @ 2.90GHz (12 threads) - 23.39 GiB memory ### Issue description Ever since I started using Godot on Linux (Wayland) I've been experiencing seemingly inconsistent freezing behavior in newly open windows (i.e. project settings window), either while trying to close the window or sometimes additionally when a tooltip is displayed and removed (i.e. when quickly hovering over something and moving the cursor) This seems to happen mainly if I attempt to use the GUI buttons and not close the window via the title bar. i.e. the cancel button when creating nodes. Unfortunately this behavior is inconsistent and I can't find any way to trigger this consistently, it leaves no logging just freezing the entire editor instantly, but it is most consistent when hovering over something to see a tooltip and then quickly removing my cursor from it. Some extra info: - I tried both using X11 bridge and Wayland (by enabling/disabling the engine option "Prefer Wayland", but the issue persists in both.) - I'm using the open kernel Nvidia drivers. - I have never encountered such issues in other applications. - I'm using the KDE Plasma desktop environment. - Edit: this behavior is seemingly completely gone when using single window mode as it is probably related to handling of multiple windows. I'm happy to do any extra tests and share any extra information. ### Steps to reproduce (Inconsistent) - Open any window (i.e. Project Settings) - Hover over the "close" button and press it (usually happens when done in quick succession)/or hover over anything that generates any tooltip and remove cursor from it. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
